note: KSEEB (Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board) sets Class 10 (SSLC) exams; the curriculum and textbooks themselves are set by DSERT Karnataka and published by KTBS (Karnataka Textbook Society). OFFICIAL SOURCES TRIED: ktbs.kar.nic.in and dsert.kar.nic.in (and the www. variant of the former) were unreachable throughout research (connection timed out / refused on every attempt, including a direct PDF URL for Class 10 Maths found via search index — the whole kar.nic.in domain appears to be down or blocked from this environment). kseeb.karnataka.gov.in loaded but is exam-administration only (SSLC login portals, certificate applications, practical-marks entry) with no syllabus or textbook content. textbooks.karnataka.gov.in — a newer official KTBS domain — WAS reachable and lists free e-textbook PDFs for 2026-27 by class/subject/medium. Its Class 6 English-medium Mathematics PDFs (Part 1 and Part 2) were downloaded in full and their text extracted directly: this confirms Karnataka has adopted NCERT's new NCF-2023 'Ganita Prakash' Grade 6 textbook verbatim (chapters Patterns in Mathematics, Lines and Angles, Number Play, Data Handling and Presentation, Prime Time, Perimeter and Area, Fractions, Playing with Constructions, Symmetry, The Other Side of Zero) from the 2025-26 academic year onward — a materially different, newer chapter list than what most Karnataka-specific solution sites still document for Class 6 Maths. This one subject is therefore marked 'fetched:' at high confidence. Attempting the same for other subjects/grades was not practical: the other official PDFs on that same site ranged from roughly 40MB to 290MB+ each (e.g. the Class 7 Maths PDF alone reports a 291MB Content-Length) and the connection available for this research throttled to under 1 Mbps, making full-book download and extraction for all 14 remaining subject/grade combinations infeasible in the time available. EVERYTHING ELSE in this catalog is 'fetched-secondary', drawn from kseebsolutions.guru and www.kseebsolutions.com (a long-established, well-regarded Karnataka-specific solutions site, NOT a generic NCERT/CBSE mirror — confirmed Karnataka-specific by its parallel Kannada-medium chapter lists using Kannada chapter titles alongside the English ones, and by state-specific content such as Karnataka geography/history chapters absent from CBSE). Chapter lists were extracted directly from each page's structured content (English-medium section only; a parallel Kannada-medium section on the same pages was discarded) and, where a subject's chapter order was surprising, cross-checked against a second independent aggregator (careers360, byjus) before being trusted as genuine rather than an artefact of the source site's own page ordering — this confirmed, for instance, that Karnataka's Class 9 and Class 10 Mathematics really are sequenced differently from the national NCERT order (Class 10 opens with Arithmetic Progressions and Triangles rather than Real Numbers, matching a second, independent source verbatim), an AP/Telangana-style state-distinctive sequencing documented here rather than silently 'corrected' to the NCERT order. SUBJECT STRUCTURE FINDINGS: (1) Science is a SINGLE COMBINED 'Science' subject in every grade from 6 to 10 — Karnataka does NOT split Physics/Chemistry/Biology into separate books at Class 9-10 the way AP/Telangana do; this was independently confirmed by web search before extraction and matches the chapter lists gathered (Class 9-10 Science interleaves Chemistry, Biology and Physics chapters within one subject, closely tracking the pre-NCF national NCERT Class 9-10 Science sequence). (2) Social Science is one combined subject at every grade, but its internal composition grows with grade level: Class 6 is published in two numbered parts (History/Geography/Civics interleaved, not split into named disciplines); Class 7 is one continuously numbered sequence (History through Class 7, then Civics, then world Geography); Classes 8, 9 and 10 are each explicitly organised into six labelled discipline sections — History, Political Science, Sociology, Geography, Economics and Business Studies — a broader combination than CBSE's usual History+Geography+Civics+Economics, and a distinctive feature of the Karnataka syllabus. All chapters from every section are included here, renumbered into one continuous 'chapters' sequence per grade in the order the source presented the sections (this reordering into a flat index array is the only liberty taken with chapter order; titles and grouping are as sourced). (3) COMPUTER SCIENCE is intentionally OMITTED for all of Classes 6-10: the official KTBS 2026-27 textbook index for English medium lists only Mathematics, Science and Social Science (plus languages) for every one of these grades — no Computer Science or IT textbook appears anywhere in that listing — and web search confirms KSEEB Class 10 core subjects are just Mathematics, Science, Social Science and languages, with Computer Science not offered as a graded subject at this level (unlike Telangana, which does publish one). No chapter list was fabricated for it. CONFIDENCE PER GRADE/SUBJECT: Class 6 Mathematics is high confidence (official, current, directly verified). Class 6 Science and Social Science, Class 7 all three subjects, and Class 8 Mathematics and Science are moderate-to-high confidence, single-source (kseebsolutions) but internally consistent and structurally plausible against known national NCERT content for the equivalent grade. Class 8-10 Social Science and Class 9-10 Mathematics are moderate-to-high confidence, cross-verified for chapter order against a second source. Class 9-10 Science and Class 8 Social Science are moderate confidence, single-source but matching well-documented national NCERT-era chapter lists for those grades. A general caveat that applies throughout: because Karnataka is mid-rollout of NCERT's NCF-2023 textbook series (confirmed for Class 6 Mathematics, and by the national rollout timeline plausibly also underway for Class 7-8 by 2026-27), the Class 7 and Class 8 chapter lists here — sourced from a solutions site that has not yet been confirmed to reflect the newest books — may lag the very latest textbook revision for those two grades, the same way AP's catalog flagged old-vs-new syllabus circulation; Class 9-10 chapter lists reflect the long-stable pre-NCF-2023 NCERT-based curriculum which is very unlikely to have changed yet. Topic blurbs throughout are original one-sentence summaries; chapter titles and subject/discipline structure are sourced as described above.
